Title: Evaluation of requests for evaluation of the need for a full MRL evaluation for chemical-unlike biologicals
Post Text: European Medicines Agency Evaluation of requests for evaluation of the need for a full MRL evaluation for chemical-unlike biologicals This guidance outlines the procedure for the evaluation of 'chemical-unlike' biological substances to determine whether a 'no MRL required' classification is appropriate without conducting a full MRL evaluation. Procedure scope: The procedure covers the evaluation of 'chemical-unlike' biological substances in accordance with Commission Regulation (EU) 2018/782 to determine if a 'no MRL required' classification is appropriate without a full MRL evaluation. Definitions: Definitions are provided for key roles involved in the application process, including the Applicant, PC, CVMP Committee for Veterinary Medicinal Products, and various support roles (P3). Process flow: A process map outlines the steps from appointing a procedure team and rapporteur to the evaluation phase, including validation steps (P4). Pre-submission phase: The pre-submission phase involves receiving the letter of intent, appointing the team, and notifying the applicant of the appointed rapporteur and submission dates. Initial evaluation: The evaluation phase includes notifying the applicant of the clock start and sending assessment report templates to the rapporteur, followed by an initial evaluation within 60 days. Conclusion decision: The CVMP can make a recommendation on the need for an MRL evaluation, leading to subsequent steps depending on the outcome. MRL recommendation: If the CVMP concludes a full assessment of the MRL is required, the applicant is informed that the procedure for evaluation must follow. Final assessment: The process includes finalizing the assessment report and opinion for endorsement by the CVMP according to the procedure steps. Title: Evaluation procedure for applications and requests for the establishment or review of Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs)
Post Text: European Medicines Agency Evaluation procedure for applications and requests for the establishment or review of Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) This guidance outlines the evaluation procedure for applications and requests concerning the establishment or review of Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) under Regulation (EC) No 470/2009. Applicant definition: An applicant is defined as a person submitting an application for MRLs under Article 3, 10, or 15 of Regulation (EC) No 470/2009, which also includes Member States or the European Commission when submitting requests under Articles 9, 11, or 27. Procedure timelines: Timelines for accelerated procedures are specified in brackets following standard procedure timelines, such as 120 (90) days. Responsibility assignment: The Head of the Veterinary Evaluation and Innovation Support Department is responsible for ensuring adherence to the procedure within their department or service; execution responsibility is detailed in section 9. Pre-submission steps: The pre-submission phase involves checking a checklist, appointment of rapporteurs, agreeing on a start date, and validation. Initial evaluation timeframe: The initial evaluation must occur within 120 (90) days following procedural steps described in the checklist. Initial evaluation monitoring: Monitoring is required for the timely receipt of draft assessment reports, critiques, and comments from peer reviewers and CVMP members. Second evaluation conclusion: The conclusion of the second evaluation phase involves agreeing on the need for an oral explanation by the CVMP at Day 180 (119). Re-examination request: A notification to request re-examination must be received within a 15-day deadline to proceed to the next steps. Title: Preparation of ESUAvet annual reports
Post Text: European Medicines Agency Preparation of ESUAvet annual reports This guidance covers inspection scope, working group change, scientific lead role. Inspection Scope: The guideline covers the preparation, conduct, reporting, and follow-up of national competent authority pharmacovigilance inspections. Working Group Change: The sign-off process has been revised, and the ESUAvet Working Group has been replaced by the ESUAvet network. Scientific Lead Role: The Scientific Lead in V-SR-AMR is situated within the Veterinary Antimicrobial Monitoring and Resistance Service in V-SR. Planning Cycle: Planning for the reporting cycle framework, including scope implementation, timelines, and risk identification, occurs in Q1 of each year. Data Monitoring: Validated quantitative data and qualitative information from Member States are monitored in Q2 of each year. Report Drafting: Relevant quantitative and qualitative data are selected for the annual report in July/August, and analytical outputs are generated. Draft Submission: Drafts are submitted to the ESUAvet network for comments in September/October to refine analyses and prevent over-interpretation. Final Sign-off: Internal sign-off by HSer, HDep, and HDiv is arranged one to two weeks before publication, with final submission to CVMP by the December meeting. Title: Processing requests for inclusion in the list of substances not falling within the scope of Regulation EC 470/2009 (out of scope) Applies to: Veterinary Medicines
Post Text: European Medicines Agency Processing requests for inclusion in the list of substances not falling within the scope of Regulation EC 470/2009 (out of scope) Applies to: Veterinary Medicines This guidance provides guidance on the management and assessment of requests for inclusion of a substance in the list of substances considered not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, which pertains to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin. Guidance purpose: This WIN provides guidance on the management and assessment of requests for inclusion of a substance in the list of substances considered not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009. Applicable staff: The WIN applies to staff members of the Veterinary Pharmaceuticals service in the Veterinary Evaluation and Innovation Support department working on requests for 'out of scope'. Required documents: Documents needed for a request include the substance list, a guideline on data provision, a procedure checklist, and a tracking table. Request handling steps: The procedure involves receiving the request, appointing a team, checking documentation against guidelines, and updating tracking tables. CVMP reporting: The procedure includes preparing and sharing a draft CVMP report for review and agreement. List revision: If a CVMP recommendation is made, the 'out of scope list' document is revised with a new revision number. Publication steps: Following the CVMP meeting, changes are accepted, and the revised list is published, with notification sent to the EC and EFTA. Applicant outcome: The applicant is informed of the CVMP outcome, which may be inclusion in the list or a recommendation for further action. Title: Provision of CVMP scientific advice
Post Text: European Medicines Agency Provision of CVMP scientific advice This guidance outlines the procedures and timelines for processing scientific advice requests under the Regulation (EU) 2019/6 on veterinary medicinal products, detailing required documents, the process map, and report distribution. Documents needed: Documents required for scientific advice include the Checklist for processing scientific advice requests, the CVMP scientific advice tracking table, and templates for scientific advice procedures. Procedure flow: The process map involves receipt/validation, inclusion in SAWP-V mailing, financial confirmation, and inclusion in the tracking table. Timeline duration: The default timetable for a scientific advice procedure is 60 days, which may be extended to 90 days for requests with high complexity. Request validation: Validation of a request involves checking if questions are presented in a clear, unambiguous manner and within the scope of the procedure. Coordinator appointment: Day 0 of the procedure requires consideration at the SAWP-V meeting for the appointment of a coordinator and agreement on the timetable. Report distribution: The final scientific advice report is included in the SAWP-V post-PC meeting mailing and circulated to consulted parties. Clarification requests: A requester may send a clarification request within six months after the scientific advice is given. Clarification response: The coordinator must prepare a draft response to a clarification request in time for a subsequent SAWP-V/CVMP meeting. Title: Organisation of CVMP Working Party meetings Applies to: Veterinary Medicines Division
Post Text: European Medicines AgencyOrganisation of CVMP Working Party meetings Applies to: Veterinary Medicines Division This guidance outlines procedures for the organisation and communication surrounding CVMP Working Party meetings, including roles, scheduling, and documentation management. Working Party Structure: The CVMP structure includes several Working Parties such as the Novel Therapies and Technologies Working Party (NTWP), Pharmacovigilance Working Party (PhVWP-V), Safety Working Party (SWP-V), and Scientific Advice Working Party (SAWP-V) (P2). Meeting Booking: Physical meeting room bookings must be made one year in advance, and meeting patterns should align with established patterns for different working parties. Meeting Request Timing: A meeting request should be submitted 8-4 weeks before the meeting for physical meetings, and virtual meeting setups require a Teams link. Participant Numbers: Participant numbers vary significantly across Working Parties, with PhVWP-V having 35 participants and SAWP-V having 16 participants (P4). Declaration of Interest: A check for the Declaration of Interest (DoI) status of all Working Party members and experts must be performed using the Expert Management Tool (EMT) before sending invitations. Invitation Timing: Invitations for physical meetings should be sent at the latest 8 weeks before the meeting, while virtual invitations can be sent up to 3 weeks in advance. First Mailing: The first mailing should be sent two weeks before the meeting, with documents indicated as 'To be circulated' if not yet available. Final Documentation: The final documentation package, including the final agenda, is tabled in the Meeting Management System (MMD) and made available to WP members after the meeting. Title: SOPP 8212: Breakthrough Therapy Products - Designation and Management
Post Text: FDA SOPP 8212: Breakthrough Therapy Products - Designation and Management This SOPP covers rescinding designation, rescind criteria, periodic reviews. Rescinding Designation: The process involves notifying senior management that the product development program no longer meets the criteria for breakthrough therapy designation, and an Intent to Rescind letter will be issued to the sponsor. Rescind Criteria: CBER may rescind the designation if the sponsor fails to submit additional justification or supportive data or request a meeting within 60 days of receiving the Intent to Rescind letter. Periodic Reviews: Periodic reviews must occur at least annually to assess the continued adequacy of the proposed overall product development plan to support an expedited development program. Review Team Composition: The review team should involve senior managers and experienced staff in a collaborative, cross-disciplinary review, assigning a project lead to facilitate the review. Meeting Planning: Multidisciplinary meetings should include the proposed timing and frequency of future meetings, information requests, and submissions related to the product development program. Data Requirements: Required data includes the status of clinical trials, preliminary evidence of effectiveness, and safety profiles across various systems. PK/PD Data: Specific requirements include justification for dose selections, information on specific populations, and clinical pharmacology, pharmacodynamic, and pharmacokinetic trials. Nonclinical Strategy: Nonclinical strategies cover completed and planned studies, including toxicology, genetic toxicology, and manufacturing process comparisons. Title: SOPP 8215: Management of Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy Products: Request for Designation, Sponsor Interactions, and Status Assessment
Post Text: FDA SOPP 8215: Management of Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy Products: Request for Designation, Sponsor Interactions, and Status Assessment This SOPP outlines the procedures for managing Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) Products, detailing the framework for supporting and monitoring the accelerated development of regenerative therapies while maintaining rigorous eligibility standards. RMAT Scope: The SOPP covers procedures for reviewing requests for RMAT designation submitted via an IND or amendment, requests to withdraw designation, related meetings, and periodic summary reviews for the designation. RMAT Eligibility: A regenerative medicine therapy must be a cell therapy, tissue engineering product, human cell/tissue product, or combination product, and must target serious/life-threatening conditions with preliminary evidence of addressing unmet needs. Submission Rules: Sponsors may request RMAT designation with an IND or amendment, ideally by the end-of-phase 2 meeting. Decision Timeline: CBER will notify the sponsor within 60 calendar days regarding whether the RMAT designation has been granted. New Request Criteria: If a request is denied due to insufficient evidence, submitting new clinical data constitutes a new designation request; sponsors may request reconsideration based on the denial rationale within 60 days. IND Amendments Review: IND amendments related to RMAT products receive expedited review, generally within 60 days, unless statutory or regulatory exceptions apply. Designation Rescission: CBER may rescind designation if criteria are no longer met; sponsors have 60 days to submit additional justification or request a meeting to support continuation. Development Communication: CBER communicates with sponsors outside critical milestone meetings to provide intensive, discipline-focused guidance on development data and milestones. Title: SOPP 8216: Fast Track Development Programs - Designation and Management
Post Text: FDA SOPP 8216: Fast Track Development Programs - Designation and Management This SOPP covers eligibility criteria, designation basis, designation scope. Eligibility Criteria: Fast Track designation is granted if a product is intended for the treatment of a serious or life-threatening disease and demonstrates the potential to address unmet medical needs for such a disease or condition. Designation Basis: CBER includes a written description of the rationale for the decision in the non-designation letter when granting Fast Track designation. Designation Scope: The designation applies to a single product and a single indication per request. Expedited Actions: Features of Fast Track designation include actions to expedite development and review, such as frequent interactions with the review team and potential for priority review. Review Process: Review team members participate in meetings and consult with subject matter experts when necessary to facilitate efficient review. Rescission Trigger: CBER may rescind the designation if the criteria for Fast Track designation are no longer met. Rescission Timeline: If a sponsor fails to submit additional justification or data within 60 days of receiving the Intent to Rescind letter, CBER may rescind the designation. Sponsor Response: Upon receiving an Intent to Rescind letter, the sponsor must respond with additional information and data, and meetings may be scheduled. Title: Safety Reporting in clinical trials
Post Text: Swissmedic Safety Reporting in clinical trials This guidance covers susar reporting, atmp definition, susar criteria. SUSAR Reporting: All Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) in clinical trials of categories B and C at Swiss trial centres must be reported to Swissmedic. This requires fulfilling three criteria: serious, related, and unexpected based on the Reference Safety Information [RSI]. Notification must include a completed submission form and a CIOMS form with participant details, medication information,, ATMP definition: ATMPs include transplant products, gene therapy products, and other nucleic acid-based products, and also products where genetic information is introduced into somatic cells, such as oligonucleotides, vectors, mRNA (including vaccines), and antisense RNA. SUSAR criteria: A Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) requires the fulfillment of three criteria: seriousness, relatedness, and unexpectedness based on the Reference Safety Information (RSI). SUSAR relatedness: In clinical trials with ATMPs, relatedness extends beyond the ATMP itself to include interventions associated with it, such as events during donation or administration. Comparator reporting: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions associated with comparator products or placebos follow the same reporting requirements as the test Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP). SUSAR timelines: Fatal and life-threatening SUSARs require initial notification within 7 days, with a follow-up report within 8 days after initial notification. Urgent safety measures: Sponsors must immediately report new events that could put trial participant safety at risk and report urgent safety measures (USMs) within 7 working days if permitted radiation dose guidance values are exceeded. Annual safety reports: Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSURs must include new SUSARs and an updated statement from the Sponsor on the benefit/risk ratio of the trial.
